Kurinji: safety that expands your world. A privacy-focused safety app designed with women at the centre, built in phases as a final-year B.Tech project. Safe enough to live. Free enough to grow.
This build has real accounts (with password change and account deletion), a Safety Circle, a manual SOS session, Safe Walk with check-ins and movement checks, Nearby (anonymous place signals) and "Check the way". Nobody can use Kurinji to track another person. During SOS or a Safe Walk, your location can be saved to your own records. Your Safety Circle is texted from your phone only if you switch on automatic SMS. During an active SOS you can record audio, photos or video as evidence: only when you tap, always with a visible notification, encrypted on your phone at once and uploaded to your private Evidence Vault. Kurinji never contacts emergency services and never records in the background on its own.
Suggested recovery passphrases use the EFF Large Wordlist by the Electronic Frontier Foundation (CC BY 3.0). Passphrases are checked against the 10k-most-common password list from the SecLists project (MIT licence).

Kurinji is a student prototype, not a released product, and there are no final terms of use yet. It is not an emergency service: it never contacts the police, an ambulance or anyone else for you, and an SMS that was sent is not proof that it was delivered or read. In an emergency, call 112 or your local emergency number. Do not rely on Kurinji as your only way to get help. Terms of use will be written and reviewed before any public release.

Privacy notice for this prototype build. It describes what this build actually does. It is written by the project team, is not legal advice and is not a final privacy policy.
Who can see your data: you, and the people who run the Kurinji server (the project team). Nobody else can look you up, follow you or see where you are: Kurinji has no family, partner or guardian mode, no location on request and no remote view, by design. Kurinji has no advertising and no analytics, and does not read your phone\'s contacts or messages.
Account: Kurinji sends your name, email and password to the Kurinji server to create and check your account. The server stores your name and email, and only a one-way hash of your password. This device stores your name, email and a sign-in token so you stay signed in (the token is not yet encrypted on the phone; a known limitation). Failed sign-ins are counted in the server\'s memory for 15 minutes only, never stored. Changing your password signs out every other phone. Asking to delete your account starts a 7-day wait; after it, everything your account holds on the server is deleted (see the end of this notice).
Location: only while an emergency is active, and only if you allow it, your phone\'s location (with its accuracy and the battery level) is saved to your own emergency record on the Kurinji server. Only you can see the saved points; the only place your location goes beyond that is a map link in the Safety Circle SMS, and only if you switch on automatic SMS or send it yourself (see below). Points that are waiting to be uploaded are kept in memory, not stored on the phone. Location points are deleted together with the emergency record and your account.
SOS without internet: an SOS starts on your phone at once, even without a connection, and is recorded on the server as soon as it can be reached. Until then the phone keeps only a random reference for the SOS, its start and end times and whether you tapped Call 112 (no location, no number); the server stores the reference and marks the times as your phone\'s. Signing out deletes what is still waiting.
Safe Walk: the server stores the walk (optional destination text you type, check-in times, missed check-ins) and only the LATEST location of your phone during the walk, which replaces the previous one. No route or track is kept. Nobody is contacted unless you switch on automatic SMS (see below).
Stop and route checks (if switched on): the destination text you type is looked up with your phone\'s map service (Google on most phones) and its coordinates are stored with the walk. Your phone compares its position with the direct route in memory only; no movement history is stored on the phone or the server. When a walk ends normally, its destination coordinates and last location are deleted from the server; if it ended in an emergency they are kept with that walk.
Safety Circle SMS (only if you switch on automatic SMS, or when you tap Text yourself): your phone sends an SMS to your enabled contacts with your name, the time, what happened and a map link to your last location. To work without internet, your enabled contacts\' names and numbers are kept on this phone (deleted when you log out). The server records only that a message was sent, to which contact and its status; never the number or the text. Tapping Call 112 opens your phone\'s dialer; Kurinji records that it was opened, not whether you called.
Evidence Vault (only during an active SOS, only when you tap): audio from your microphone, or a photo or video taken with your phone\'s own camera app. Each item is encrypted on this phone right away with its own key, which is protected by your phone\'s secure hardware; the unencrypted file is deleted. The Kurinji server receives only the encrypted file, its size, two fingerprints (SHA-256), the capture times and a chain-of-custody log; it cannot open the evidence. If the server offers a vault recovery key, a copy of each item\'s key is sealed for it, so the evidence can still be recovered if your phone is lost; that recovery key is kept offline by the Kurinji operator, not on the server. If you set up a recovery passphrase, the server also stores a copy of each item\'s key locked with a key that only your passphrase opens; the passphrase itself never leaves your phone, so Kurinji cannot read it or reset it (someone holding the server\'s data could try to guess a weak passphrase, which is why short or common ones are refused). The server records when that locked copy was last fetched. No location, file name or device details are sent with evidence. You can delete evidence everywhere with your password once the emergency has ended. The camera app you use may keep its own copy; check its settings.
Nearby (only when you open it): your phone turns one location fix into an area code of about 1 km to look at your area, and of about 150 m to report or answer. Your coordinates never leave the phone. A report says only the kind of place problem (or a safe place) and that block; it has no text, photo, name or time, and nobody is shown who shared it. It starts to count after a random delay, shows only to about 1 km until a second person confirms it, and is deleted at the end of its lifetime. You can see and withdraw your own reports in Nearby. Privately, the server keeps a few counters about how your reports turned out (never places or times); they halve every 90 days and are never shown, not even to you. If you flag a signal, a moderator sees only codes and a pseudonym valid for that one case. Moderation decisions are logged with reason codes for 365 days.
Check the way (Safe Walk set-up): your phone asks for area summaries of a few regions of about 5 km; the server never receives your route or destination, and nothing is stored.
Counts: once a week the server counts, system-wide, how the Nearby rules worked (no person, place or signal). Only an administrator can read them.
Rise: everything you write or choose in Rise (goals, steps, how you expected and how it went, dates) stays on this phone in a file encrypted with a key held by your phone\'s secure hardware, separately for each account. None of it is sent to the Kurinji server or to anyone. Rise has no reminders or notifications. Signing out keeps it; Delete all Rise data, deleting your account, or uninstalling the app removes it.
Account deletion: you need your password; it is refused during an emergency and for 24 hours after one, and it waits 7 days (cancel with your password; signing in does not cancel it). Then the server deletes your account and everything it holds: emergencies and their locations, walks, Safety Circle, evidence files and records, recovery data and Nearby contributions. If you ever acted as a moderator, your account row stays as an anonymous, switched-off record so that the moderation log keeps who decided what; your name, email and safety data are still deleted. After the deletion, this phone removes the account\'s evidence and recovery key the next time it learns of it, or when you tap the button on the login screen.
Retention in short: emergency locations, walks and evidence stay until you delete them or your account; walk destinations and last locations are deleted when a walk ends normally; Nearby signals expire on their own; moderation log 365 days; weekly counts 104 weeks.
A complete privacy policy will be written and reviewed before any public release.
